problem: Visual semantic navigation typically uses a single agent or several homogeneous agents, which suffer from limited perception and inefficient exploration when searching for multiple semantic targets in complex indoor scenes.
motivation: Agents with different perceptual capabilities can complement each other, so fusing their observations could make multi-target search faster and more robust under uncertainty. The paper proposes a heterogeneous multi-agent setup to exploit this (based on the abstract only).
key_idea: Heterogeneous agents periodically fuse local observations into a unified global semantic map, and a frontier-based exploration strategy with centralized task allocation drives efficient multi-target search.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or analysis could be read. The abstract claims that complementary perception across heterogeneous agents, together with shared mapping and central allocation, improves success rate and path efficiency over single-agent baselines.
method: Heterogeneous multi-agent system: agents with complementary perceptual capabilities explore the same environment.
Global semantic map fusion: local observations are periodically fused into a unified global semantic map.
Frontier-based exploration: agents select frontiers on the shared map to explore.
Centralized task allocation: a central planner assigns targets/frontiers to agents for multi-target search.

setting.observation: not specified (visual and semantic cues; local observations fused into a global semantic map)

results: The abstract states that in complex unseen indoor environments the method achieves higher task success rates and improved path efficiency than traditional single-agent baselines. No numbers are given.
limitations: Only compared against single-agent baselines according to the abstract; no comparison to homogeneous multi-agent methods is mentioned.
Relies on centralized allocation and periodic map fusion, which assumes reliable communication.
